title: Data-Free Transition-Spectrum Winsorization for Mamba Long-Context Generalization

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to extend Mamba's long-context generalization without requiring calibration data. Papers [1], [2], [5], [6], [8], [9], [13], and [16] all address improving Mamba's long-context capabilities or length generalization, but they do not explicitly focus on achieving this without calibration data. Paper [10] discusses training-free long-context extrapolation for LLMs, which aligns with the goal of avoiding calibration data, but it is specific to LLMs rather than Mamba. No prior paper explicitly combines the purpose of extending Mamba's long-context generalization with the constraint of avoiding calibration data.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves transition-spectrum winsorization, which clips extreme eigenvalues (outside the [q, 1-q] percentile range) in each layer's transition spectrum while preserving the mid-spectrum. Papers [12], [14], [15], [17], [19], and [21] discuss winsorization techniques, including its application to eigenvalues and robustness in various contexts. Paper [17] specifically explores winsorized PCA for subspace recovery, which involves eigenvalue manipulation. While none of these papers apply winsorization to Mamba's transition spectrum, the underlying primitive of clipping extreme eigenvalues is substantively equivalent.

### Evaluation
The evaluation design involves measuring perplexity (PPL) on PG-19 with Mamba2-1.3B, comparing performance against constant scaling and calibrated scaling. Papers [1], [2], [5], [6], [8], [9], [13], and [16] all evaluate Mamba's long-context capabilities using perplexity or similar metrics on long-context benchmarks. While the specific dataset (PG-19) and model instance (Mamba2-1.3B) differ, the evaluation design — comparing long-context performance using perplexity — is covered by these prior works.

### Domain
The domain is the long-context extension of Mamba/state space models. Papers [1], [2], [5], [6], [8], [9], [13], and [16] all operate in the same general application area of improving Mamba's long-context capabilities or length generalization. While specific sub-problems or datasets may differ, the domain is clearly covered.

This mechanism combines: (a) eigenvalue/spectral analysis of SSM/recurrent model transition matrices, and (b) winsorization applied to that spectrum. ### Purpose
The purpose of the contribution is to show that targeted clipping (e.g., winsorization of extreme eigenvalues) outperforms uniform scaling in terms of reducing short-context regression. None of the prior papers explicitly establish or report this specific empirical relationship. While several papers discuss winsorization (e.g., [3], [8], [19], [24]) or clipping (e.g., [2], [7], [13]), none of them compare targeted clipping against uniform scaling or demonstrate that targeted clipping achieves better performance in this context. Therefore, the purpose is **not covered**.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves comparing winsorization of extreme eigenvalues (modifying 17.5% of channels) against uniform constant scaling (100% of channels). Winsorization is explicitly discussed in [3], [8], [19], and [24], and uniform scaling is discussed in [2] and [7]. Paper [13] investigates spectrum clipping in learning stable linear dynamics, which is conceptually similar to the winsorization of eigenvalues. However, none of these papers directly compare winsorization to uniform scaling in the same way as the contribution. Thus, while the individual components of the mechanism are covered, the specific comparison is **not covered**.

### Evaluation
The evaluation demonstrates that targeted clipping outperforms uniform scaling with lower short-context regression (+6.8% vs +20.8%). Papers [3], [8], [19], and [24] discuss winsorization and its effects, but they do not use the same evaluation design or metrics as this contribution. Similarly, papers [2], [7], and [13] discuss clipping or scaling but do not evaluate their methods in terms of short-context regression or a comparable metric. Therefore, the evaluation design is **not covered**.

### Domain
The domain is the long-context extension of Mamba/state space models. Papers [1], [10], [12], and [17] all address long-context modeling in state space models or related architectures. For example, [1] applies Mamba to speech recognition, [10] characterizes state space models and hybrid models for long-context tasks, [12] investigates length extension in state space models, and [17] introduces spectral state space models for long-range dependencies. These papers collectively establish that the domain of long-context modeling in state space models is well-covered. Thus, the domain is **covered**.
